title: GET /api/dashboard/metrics runs its ~12 sub-aggregations concurrently via Promise.all
description: dashboard-metrics/index.js's /metrics handler issues projects, compliance, resources, findings, risk overview, risk-level distribution, vendor, audit, RMS posture/governance, audit-assurance metrics, vendor-assessment metrics, and SLA-breach count all inside a single Promise.all — total latency should track the slowest sub-query, not their sum.
steps: Instrument or profile a cache-miss call to GET /api/dashboard/metrics on a representative-sized org
Compare total handler latency to the sum of each individual sub-query's latency measured in isolation
expectedResult: Total handler latency is close to the single slowest sub-query's latency (allowing for overhead), not the sum of all sub-queries — confirming they run in parallel rather than sequentially.

title: A repeated /api/dashboard/metrics call within the cache TTL never touches MongoDB
description: dashboard-cache.js's EXEC_DASH_CACHE_TTL defaults to 60 seconds. A second identical-params request inside that window should be served purely from Redis.
steps: Call GET /api/dashboard/metrics once (cache miss, populates Redis)
Call it again immediately with identical query params, while monitoring MongoDB query logs/profiler
expectedResult: The second call returns the identical payload with zero new MongoDB queries logged, and observably lower latency than the first call.

title: A slow or failed trend endpoint doesn't block the main metrics response from rendering
description: AuditOverviewContent's fetchMetrics fires the main dashboardService.getDashboardMetrics() call alongside 5 trend calls (risk/audit/vendor/framework/resource) via Promise.allSettled — a rejection or timeout on any one trend call must not prevent the main KPI cards from rendering.
steps: Simulate executiveVendorBoardService.getVendorTrends timing out or returning an error
expectedResult: All 6 KPI cards still render with their headline values populated; only the Vendor Board's sparkline falls back to the honest empty/placeholder state, and no page-level error is shown.

title: A large project-scope selection produces a fixed-size Redis cache key regardless of project count
description: dashboard-cache.js's buildKey hashes the sorted params object with MD5 and truncates to 12 hex characters, so an org with hundreds of active projects selected via ?projectIds= doesn't produce an oversized Redis key.
preconditions: An org (or synthetic test org) with 200+ active projects, all selected via ?projectIds=
steps: Inspect the resulting Redis key via redis-cli KEYS 'exec-dash:*'
expectedResult: The key matches exec-dash:{orgId}:dashboard-metrics:{12-hex-char-hash} regardless of how many project IDs were in the params — key length does not grow with project count.

title: Finding totals/severity breakdown/critical count are computed in a single $facet pass
description: dashboard-metrics/index.js's Finding aggregation uses one $facet stage (total, bySeverity, critical) rather than three separate aggregate calls, avoiding three full collection scans on orgs with very large Finding collections.
steps: On an org with a large (100k+) Finding collection, profile GET /api/dashboard/metrics
Inspect the MongoDB query log/explain output for the Finding aggregation
expectedResult: Exactly one aggregate() call against the Finding collection is logged (using $facet), not three separate ones for total/bySeverity/critical.

title: Switching the module rail unmounts the previously-selected board instead of leaving it mounted and polling in the background
description: AuditOverviewContent wraps the board content in <AnimatePresence mode='wait'> with a single <motion.div key={selectedBoard}>, so only one board's content component is ever mounted at a time — switching boards fully unmounts the previous one (and its own internal data-fetch effects/intervals) rather than hiding it in place.
steps: Open Audit Board and let its data finish loading
Switch to Vendor Board via the module rail
Monitor the Network tab for any further requests originating from Audit Board’s own services
expectedResult: No further network requests attributable to Audit Board fire after switching away from it — confirming its component (and any interval/effect it owned) was actually unmounted, not merely hidden.

title: PriorityActionsPanel skips a redundant refetch when projectIds is set to an identical value
description: PriorityActionsPanel.jsx guards its fetch effect with lastKeyRef, comparing JSON.stringify(projectIds) against the previous call's key and returning early on a match — avoiding a duplicate /priority-actions request when the parent re-renders with a new array identity but the same underlying project IDs.
steps: Trigger a parent re-render of AuditOverviewContent that produces a new selectedProjectIds array instance with the same string values (e.g. an unrelated state update)
expectedResult: No additional /priority-actions request fires for a re-render that carries the same project IDs, even if the array reference itself changed.
